comparator.name: Computing Science (Informatica)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current UvA curriculum page gives two 60-EC compulsory years. Year 1 combines programming, computer architecture, data structures, web technology, programming languages, discrete mathematics and logic, linear algebra, operating systems, Internet of Things and two academic-skills components. Year 2 adds databases, networks and security, distributed and parallel programming, statistics, a numerical project, algorithms and complexity, computer vision, automata and formal languages, reflection on digital society, software engineering and two academic-skills components. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine open elective space, a 12-EC restricted choice of two out of three named courses, and an 18-EC bachelor project. Compiler Construction and Classical Cryptography are selected as the first two officially listed restricted choices; Theory of Functional Programming is not combined with them. The overview confirms a Dutch-taught, full-time 180-EC BSc under RIO code 56978.

alternatives.concept: Builds a UCR computing programme around programming, networks and operating systems, databases, software development, algorithms and mathematical foundations, with data and AI applications. UCR covers substantial computer-science content but has less structured hardware, security, parallel-systems and formal research training than UvA.

alternatives.concept: Uses the same programming and systems foundation, then emphasizes numerical methods, linear systems, calculus, optimization, machine learning, robotics and human-centred AI. This is a mathematical and modelling direction within computing rather than a claim to reproduce UvA's full systems curriculum.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme and a 30-EC-distinct mathematical and intelligent-systems direction are feasible. All remaining generator-eligible interests concern the same computer-science core, software and systems emphasis, or are already represented by these two programmes. Curricular topics such as graphics, games, security and human-computer interaction strengthen the map but cannot independently generate a third alternative, and UCR does not offer a coherent specialist sequence in those areas.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Programming directly addresses the UvA introductory programming component, with different scope and credits.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics addresses the UvA discrete mathematics and logic component, with different scope and credits.
Linear Algebra directly addresses the UvA linear algebra component, with different scope and credits.
Computational & Numerical Methods addresses the numerical-computation function of the UvA Numerical Recipes Project, while UvA organizes it as a project.
Probability & Statistics addresses the statistical reasoning component, with a more mathematical emphasis and different credits.
Algorithms & Data Structures directly addresses the UvA data-structures component, with different scope and credits.
Advanced Algorithms addresses the algorithms and complexity component, with different scope and credits.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces the UvA automata and formal-languages component.
Networks & Operating Systems directly addresses the operating-systems component and also includes network foundations, with different scope and credits.
Database Management Systems directly addresses the UvA modern-databases component, with different scope and credits.
Software Development addresses software design, testing and maintenance central to the UvA software-engineering project, though UvA uses a dedicated project format.
The Art of Rhetorical Communication addresses the communication function of one UvA academic-skills component, but is not computer-science-specific.
AI Ethics addresses the ethical and societal reflection function of Reflectie op de Digitale Samenleving, with a narrower AI focus.
UCR has no selected course equivalent to the historical and disciplinary survey Keerpunten in de Informatiewetenschappen.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces computer architecture and organization.
UCR has no selected dedicated web-technology course.

notes.text: The UvA degree requires computer architecture, web technology, programming languages, operating systems, Internet of Things, networks and security, distributed and parallel programming, automata and formal languages, a software-engineering project, selected compiler construction and cryptography, and an 18-EC final project. UCR can build a substantial programme in programming, databases, networks and operating systems, algorithms, mathematics, data science and AI, but it does not reproduce this complete structured systems and research sequence.
